The bottleneck for software engineering keeps changing.

Historically, it was writing the code and tests to ensure they conformed with the specs.

In early days of agentic coding it was reviewing code for correctness.

Now (for complex projects) it's the build & test phase.

It's rather frustrating when you can make significant code changes in 10 minutes but then it takes an hour or more to find out if it passes QA.

The bottleneck for software engineering keeps changing.

Historically, it was writing the code and tests to ensure they conformed with the specs.

In early days of agentic coding it was reviewing code for correctness.

Now (for complex projects) it's the build & test phase.

It's rather frustrating when you can make significant code changes in 10 minutes but then it takes an hour or more to find out if it passes QA.

I'm sure folks will apply AI to improve the efficiency of their CI/CD pipelines, but part of the problem is that due to the nature of agentic coding you want even more tests than ever before in order to ensure correctness, and then those tests necessarily take more time and resources to run every time you ship new code.

@jeremytwei Of course, though that just gets annoying because then you have a set up a bunch of separate workspaces so that they can all be running in parallel.

And gave PTSD to Google executives over from his leadership at $NVDA:

Was that if a critical material can be bought out for spare change eg. ~$400m (FY2028 Photonics-SOI revenue forecast for $SOI)

We're going to see game theory bottleneck supply procurement actually accelerate upstream through 2027, with or without him.

Deleveraging/negative sentiment is indiscriminately moving the theme up and down together, so hard to argue individual fundamentals at this point. 

Reflecting on 2026, I also prob need to be more selective of companies entering 2027:

But there's going to be a lot of outsized opportunities in bottlenecks... as new architectures like NPO/CPO emerge across the ecosystem.
